stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The associated tags confirm its relevance within the transformer and Llama ecosystem.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
The model is optimized for local coding agents and features native support for DFlash and image input via Ollama's MLX engine.

stories.title: Run Qwen 3.8 Flash Next (125B) on consumer hardware (RTX 4090) at 100T/s
stories.author: snehesht
bullet_points: Demonstrates the feasibility of running a massive LLM (Qwen 3.8 Flash, 125B parameters) on high-end consumer GPUs (RTX 4090).
Achieves a high inference throughput of 100T/s, indicating significant performance gains for local LLM deployment.
Suggests a major shift towards democratizing large-scale AI by enabling powerful models on consumer hardware.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text-generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The associated tags confirm its relevance within the broader transformer and LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now available via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model with 3B active parameters.
The model is specifically designed for persistent AI agents capable of multi-step tasks and tool calling on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance shows up to a 90% speed increase when benchmarked using Aider.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Apple changes full-disk access permissions to curb abuse from AI agents
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Apple is modifying full-disk access permissions to mitigate potential misuse by AI agents.
The change addresses concerns over AI agents accessing sensitive user data, such as private messages.
The article highlights a disagreement between Apple and Meta regarding the adequacy of existing regulatory frameworks (like the FDA) for controlling AI behavior.

stories.title: EyeRobot 2.0: Active Gaze for Precise Manipulation without Wrist Cameras
stories.author: Angjoo Kanazawa
bullet_points: Introduces EyeRobot 2.0, a framework for fine-grained bimanual manipulation.
Achieves precise manipulation using only a single stereo camera by employing active gaze.
Utilizes Active Visual Fixation (AVF) to focus computational resources by allocating more visual tokens to the foveal region.

stories.title: Transcriptome-informed multi-modal AI for predicting neoadjuvant therapy response from breast cancer biopsies
stories.author: Krzysztof J. Geras
bullet_points: Introduces a two-stage AI model to predict pathological complete response (pCR) in breast cancer.
Addresses data scarcity in oncology by learning transcriptome features from histopathology across 32 cancer types.
The model infers gene expression from images, simplifying the final prediction stage using clinical variables.

stories.title: Language Models that Play Chess and Explain Their Moves
stories.author: Danqi Chen
bullet_points: Introduces 'Queen,' a 4B-parameter chess-language model designed to bridge the gap between strong chess engines and explanatory language models.
Queen achieves Grandmaster-level playing strength while simultaneously providing human-understandable explanations for its moves and strategic plans.
The research presents a novel framework enabling domain-specific reasoning by integrating language capabilities with complex game-playing AI.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free decision-making based on text input.
The models provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scoring.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary LLM interfaces with local, open-source model ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Our minds aren’t equipped to handle AI
stories.author: Benjamin Riley
bullet_points: The article discusses the philosophical and cognitive limitations of human minds in relation to advanced AI.
It references historical perspectives, citing Norbert Wiener and the concept of technology reflecting human thought.
It contrasts high-level views from AI leaders like Demis Hassabis and Elon Musk regarding the brain's relationship to computation.

stories.title: An AI couldn’t beat humans at StarCraft, so it decided to cheat
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: A competitive AI bot tournament, StarSkirmish, pits AI-generated bots against human-made ones in StarCraft.
Leading large language models like GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 were competitive but were outperformed by the human-created bot, Stardust.
The story touches on the ongoing comparison between advanced AI performance and human-designed systems in complex strategy games.

stories.title: Amazon’s $1B plan to combat data center backlash draws more backlash
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Amazon has a $1 billion initiative aimed at addressing criticism surrounding its data centers.
The company received mixed reactions, being praised for ending Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs).
However, Amazon faced further criticism for allegedly minimizing the environmental impact and pollution from its data centers.

stories.title: Less Decoder is More Encoder: Geometric Representation Learning from Novel View Synthesis
stories.author: Animesh Garg
bullet_points: The paper investigates using Novel View Synthesis (NVS) for geometric representation learning.
Existing encoder-based NVS methods produce poor 3D scene representations despite having supervisory signals.
The authors suggest that overly expressive decoders are diluting the representational power of the scene encoder.

stories.title: 4DCodeBench: Benchmarking Agents on Inverse Graphics of Dynamic Scenes
stories.author: Jiajun Wu
bullet_points: Introduces 4DCodeBench, a new benchmark for evaluating AI agents in 4D inverse graphics.
The core task involves agents reconstructing dynamic scenes from video input by generating executable graphics programs.
This requires agents to translate visual data into compact scene representations, including implementing physical simulations.

stories.title: FrugalEvo: Towards Cost-Aware LLM-Guided Program Evolution
stories.author: Bryan Hooi
bullet_points: Introduces FrugalEvo, a novel cost-aware framework for LLM-guided program evolution.
Addresses a limitation in prior work by shifting optimization focus from total performance gain to gain per unit cost.
Utilizes a hierarchical LLM approach: a high-cost LLM for strategy exploration and a low-cost LLM for implementation.

stories.title: MRVQ: One Resident Index for Dimension- and Rate-Elastic Vector Search
stories.author: Kang Li
bullet_points: Introduces MRVQ (Matryoshka Residual Vector Quantization) for efficient vector search.
Addresses the challenge of balancing latency, quality, and memory in dense-retrieval services.
Allows for dynamic rate reduction by truncating residual quantization stages without retraining.

stories.title: On-Board Anomaly Detection for Efficient Marine Environmental Monitoring
stories.author: Adrien Girard
bullet_points: Proposes an AI-driven pipeline for detecting marine environmental hazards (e.g., oil spills, algal blooms) using Earth observation satellites.
The system utilizes multi- or hyperspectral sensors and incorporates a self-supervised neural network for anomaly detection.
Addresses the critical need for early detection and mitigation of threats impacting marine ecosystems.

stories.title: Do Large Language Models Know Colombian Law? A Reliability Benchmark for the Colombian Legal System
stories.author: Joaquín Vélez Navarro
bullet_points: Introduces a novel, expert-validated benchmark to test LLM reliability specifically within the Colombian legal system.
Addresses a critical gap in current AI research: the lack of documentation regarding LLM performance in non-US national legal frameworks.
The benchmark is comprehensive, containing 1,042 items across ten legal areas and three distinct question formats (including IRAC).

stories.title: What Should World Models Forget? Stratified Retention for Continual Adaptation
stories.author: Dinesh Manocha
bullet_points: The paper addresses the limitations of traditional continual learning when applied to world models.
It argues that world models operate with a non-stationary prediction target (the environment), unlike standard ML tasks.
The research proposes 'Stratified Retention' to manage knowledge decay, viewing forgetting as necessary adaptation rather than failure.

stories.title: RNADyn: A Benchmark for Generating and Understanding RNA Dynamics
stories.author: Tolga Birdal
bullet_points: Introduction of RNADynBench, a new standardized benchmark for RNA molecular dynamics (MD).
The benchmark comprises 2585 quality-controlled 100-ns all-atom trajectories, addressing data scarcity in RNA dynamics.
The work aims to unify trajectory generation and dynamics understanding, which are often treated separately in current research.

stories.title: LESSER: Post-Training Data Selection with Output-Layer Gradients
stories.author: Anton Xue
bullet_points: The study addresses the critical issue of selecting optimal post-training data for Large Language Models (LLMs) to improve downstream performance.
Traditional gradient-based data selection methods are computationally prohibitive due to the need for expensive backward passes on large datasets.
The research proposes an approximation method to estimate full-gradient features at a fraction of the computational cost.

stories.title: Pivot-SD: Efficient Self-Distillation for Masked Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Rahul G. Krishnan
bullet_points: Introduces 'Pivot-SD,' a method for efficient self-distillation in Masked Diffusion Language Models (dLMs).
Addresses a key challenge in dLMs: the credit-assignment problem arising from early denoising commitments.
Proposes using the uncertainty signal during denoising to guide targeted training, unlike current whole-text training methods.

stories.title: Forecasting from Counterfactual Simulator Rollouts: A Sim2Real Evaluation
stories.author: Carson Eisenach
bullet_points: Addresses the 'cold-start problem' in prediction models when deploying new decision policies.
Proposes using counterfactual simulator rollouts to generate training data for the new policy.
Focuses on the Simulation-to-Reality (Sim2Real) transfer of learned policies.

stories.title: PoCoFL: POlicy-COmpliant Federated Learning
stories.author: Aysajan Abidin
bullet_points: Introduces PoCoFL, a new framework for Policy-Compliant Federated Learning (FL).
Addresses a critical gap in FL: ensuring clients submit policy-compliant contributions and aggregators process them correctly.
Overcomes the limitation of existing verifiable FL systems, which are often too tailored to specific FL settings and constructions.

stories.title: On-Board Anomaly Detection for Efficient Marine Environmental Monitoring
stories.author: Adrien Girard
bullet_points: Proposes a marine event detection pipeline for Earth observation satellites.
Utilizes AI, specifically a self-supervised neural network, for anomaly detection.
Aims to monitor and mitigate environmental threats like oil spills and algal blooms.

stories.title: FrugalEvo: Towards Cost-Aware LLM-Guided Program Evolution
stories.author: Bryan Hooi
bullet_points: Introduces FrugalEvo, a novel cost-aware framework for LLM-guided program evolution.
Addresses a limitation in prior work by optimizing for gain per unit cost rather than just performance over fixed iterations.
Utilizes a hierarchical LLM approach: a stronger, high-cost LLM for strategy exploration and a cheaper LLM for implementation.

stories.title: Pivot-SD: Efficient Self-Distillation for Masked Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Rahul G. Krishnan
bullet_points: Introduces 'Pivot-SD,' a method for efficient self-distillation in Masked Diffusion Language Models (dLMs).
Addresses the 'credit-assignment challenge' in dLMs, where early denoising steps significantly constrain subsequent token predictions.
Proposes leveraging the uncertainty signal during denoising to guide targeted training, moving beyond standard full-text training.

stories.title: World Embedding Benchmark
stories.author: Chenghao Xiao
bullet_points: Introduces the World Embedding Benchmark, a new resource for evaluating physical fidelity in AI models.
The benchmark contains 8,000 controlled simulation cases covering diverse physics domains (fluid, solid mechanics, optics, etc.).
It supports three tasks, including text-video retrieval, by pairing rendered videos with simulation-derived physical annotations.

stories.title: FALCON: A Model and Dataset Agnostic Framework for Synthetic Data Generation for NL2SQL Pairs
stories.author: Yuanming Shi
bullet_points: FALCON is a new framework designed for generating synthetic Natural Language to SQL (NL2SQL) pairs.
The framework addresses a key limitation in existing methods by handling the inherent ambiguity found in real-world natural language queries.
This research aims to improve the robustness of models used for querying structured knowledge bases (relational databases).

stories.title: Divergence controls entropy in distillation
stories.author: Scott W. Linderman
bullet_points: The paper investigates the entropic properties of knowledge distillation, a core technique in LLM training.
A key finding is that using forward KL divergence inflates the student model's entropy relative to the teacher model.
The research provides theoretical insights into distillation objectives, verifying identities in practical pretraining and finetuning.

stories.title: Huawei and Qualcomm Announce Broad Patent License Agreement
stories.author: 0xedb
bullet_points: Huawei and Qualcomm have reached a broad patent license agreement.
This agreement addresses intellectual property concerns between the two major tech players.
The news signals a potential easing or stabilization of IP disputes in the semiconductor industry.

stories.title: The Witness Was the Suspect: Why AI Audit Logs Can't Be Trusted
stories.author: james_anderson_h
bullet_points: The article addresses the critical security vulnerability of trusting AI audit logs.
It highlights scenarios where AI agents can cause significant operational errors (data leaks, database corruption).
The core theme is the need for robust verification methods beyond standard AI logging.

stories.title: Before the Alarm Screams at 3 AM: Predicting Liam's Nocturnal Hypoglycemia with Prior Labs TabPFN
stories.author: emmasofia
bullet_points: Introduces Prior Labs TabPFN, a tabular foundation model for medical prediction.
The model predicts nocturnal hypoglycemia crashes using Continuous Glucose Monitor (CGM) logs.
A key feature highlighted is the ability to operate with zero cloud data leaks, emphasizing privacy.

stories.title: He Knew Every Line of Code But Couldn't Ask for Water. I Built AphasiaBridge with Thinking Machines' Tinker to Restore My Friend's Voice in 174ms
stories.author: tahosin
bullet_points: A personal project demonstrating the application of AI/ML to solve a real-world accessibility issue (aphasia).
The solution, 'AphasiaBridge,' utilizes Thinking Machines' Tinker and Gemma-2B for voice restoration.
The system achieved a low latency of 174ms, highlighting real-time potential for assistive technology.

stories.title: We Gave AI Agents Real Tools — Then Realized “Just Ask Before Acting” Wasn’t Enough
stories.author: robertadam987_
bullet_points: The article discusses the advancement of AI agents by equipping them with functional tools.
It highlights a key realization: simple guardrails like 'ask before acting' are insufficient for complex agent behavior.
The integration of tools (like reading capabilities) is presented as a critical step toward making AI agents truly useful.
